articles.title_orig: China says US exploiting spy allegations to justify technology curbs
articles.title_zh: China says US exploiting spy allegations to justify technology curbs
articles.content_orig:
China on Thursday rejected what it called the US “Chinese spy narrative”, insisting that its technological progress was driven by independent innovation and international cooperation rather than espionage.
Foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular news briefing in Beijing amid reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could be removed following allegations of extramarital affairs, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence.
“The United States should stop fabricating the so-called Chinese spy narrative as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions,” Mao said.
“China’s scientific progress relies on independent innovation and open cooperation,” she added.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs.
The newspaper said the board was expected to meet as early as on Wednesday, US time, to discuss his future.
The New York Times separately reported that Huang had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.
Huang has previously acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, while Nvidia's board is investigating whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
Beijing addresses upcoming Trump-Xi meeting
Asked whether the controversy could affect an expected meeting between the Chinese and US presidents next week, Mao said Beijing had already made its position clear on what it described as the Chinese espionage narrative.
“China and the US remain in close communication regarding interactions between the two countries’ leaders. We stand ready to work with the US to fully implement the important consensus reached by the two presidents and advance a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” she said, according to Beijing-based newspaper Global Times .
Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to host US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen as Beijing prepares to host the annual APEC leaders' summit.
China criticises US chip export restrictions
Mao also criticised US restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports to China, accusing Washington of expanding the definition of national security to justify curbs on Chinese companies.
“We are against the US attempts to overstretch the concept of national security,” she said, denouncing what she described as discriminatory restrictions targeting Chinese firms.

articles.title_orig: Deadly Israeli air strike hits hospital, 13 killed across Gaza
articles.title_zh: Deadly Israeli air strike hits hospital, 13 killed across Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Israeli attacks have killed at least 13 Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heavy rains.
At least six Palestinians, including a doctor, were killed in an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, according to Gaza’s health ministry and civil defence. The attack in the early hours of Thursday wounded at least 20 other people.
“Most of those killed and injured were patients, including people who were scheduled to undergo surgery the following day,” said Al Jazeera’s Gaza correspondent, Hind Khoudary. Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum added that Rizk Abu Shaira, “a significant and prominent surgeon”, was among those killed.
The facility’s director, Raed al-Dahshan, said a missile penetrated the building vertically, passing through several floors and causing widespread destruction.
The strike caused significant damage to the surgery department and ICU, he said, adding that he expected the death toll to rise, given the nature of the injuries.
“This is one of the largest hospitals in the Gaza Strip and the only hospital still standing in Khan Younis, serving at least 500,000 people in southern Gaza,” Khoudary said, adding that the latest attack was the seventh time Israel struck Nasser Medical Complex in the past couple of years.
The Israeli military claimed it was targeting a Hamas commander at the hospital.
Hamas condemned the strike as a “war crime”. It also said Israel’s claim of targeting Hamas members are “nothing but a blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime committed against a civilian medical facility protected under international law”.
In an earlier statement, Hamas said: “Mediators and the US administration must take action to halt the occupation’s ongoing violations and ensure its adherence to a ceasefire.”
Israel has continued near-daily attacks despite a so-called “ceasefire” that has been in place since October 2025. Since then, at least 1,600 Palestinians ⁠⁠have been killed in Israeli attacks, Gaza’s health ministry says.
The Palestinian Islamic Jihad movement on Thursday accused US President Donald Trump’s administration of providing “political and military cover for the [Israeli] occupation”. “The policy of impunity encourages the occupation to escalate its aggression,” it said after the hospital attack.
Gaza-based political analyst Ahmed al-Tanani said Israel’s strike on Nasser Medical Complex sends a message that “there is no possibility of life and no possibility of recovery in the Gaza Strip”.
“Since the first day of the [Gaza ceasefire], the occupation [Israel] has gradually broken down its barriers”, he told Al Jazeera, noting Israel’s daily killings of Palestinians, expansion of the “yellow line”, and “now, it has reached the stage of bombing a hospital”.
Before the strike on Nasser Medical Complex, Israeli attacks killed seven other Palestinians across the Strip.
An Israeli air attack on Wednesday killed 38-year-old Mohammed Salem al-Daash in the Sabra neighbourhood, south of Gaza City.
Another Palestinian was shot and killed by Israeli forces east of the Bureij camp in central Gaza, and another was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the Nassr neighbourhood, northwest of Gaza City.
At least two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in a strike that hit a tent sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood, north of Gaza City.
Al Jazeera’s Khoudary described the Israeli attacks as the indiscriminate targeting of civilians, saying people who were carrying on with simple attempts to survive lost their lives, such as “a man filling up a water tank, [who] was killed in a drone strike”.
“In another attack, two brothers from the al-Absi family were killed while they were sheltering inside their tent on al-Jalaa Street,” she said, adding that nowhere in Gaza was safe.
The Israeli attacks came as the UN appealed for more tents to be sent to the enclave because at least 70,000 tents were flooded in weekend rains, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.
Heavy rain has directly affected at least 106,000 people in Gaza in recent days, according to the UN children’s agency, UNICEF, with thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians submerged under water and latrines overflowing into camps.
NGOs and local organisations say they do not have the resources or capacity to deal with the crisis, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of essential aid.
“Ultimately, we need the Israeli authorities to cooperate with giving the permissions so that we can bring those tents in,” UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq told reporters at a media briefing, adding that apart from funding, Israeli permits were needed “to get this in”.
Certain countries supporting aid deliveries to Gaza have said that delivering winter supplies will have to wait for the formation of an Israeli government, according to Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs.
In a statement, Fletcher said foreign ministers have assured their support, “but also repeatedly said that progress would be hard until after Israeli elections. Now we’re told to wait for the formation of a government.
“This is not an acceptable excuse,” he added, citing international law and the consequences of delays, blockages and funding cuts.
Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Wednesday that Rome has launched a new emergency initiative worth 5 million euros ($5.5m) to provide immediate assistance to the Gaza Strip following the floods.
The death toll from Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza has surged to 74,653 civilians killed since October 7, 2023, according to health authorities in Gaza.
An additional 176,007 Palestinians have been injured in the past three years. More than 5,878 people have been injured since the Gaza “ceasefire” agreement came into effect in October 2025.

articles.title_orig: Who could run Nvidia after Jensen Huang?
articles.title_zh: Who could run Nvidia after Jensen Huang?
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX founder and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said it would be "an honor" to hire embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after reports emerged that Nvidia's board could be preparing to oust Huang from the company.
Late Wednesday stateside, financial blog Zerohedge wrote on X, "Elon please hire Jensen," to which Musk replied , "That would be an honor."
The post comes as the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss Huang's future at the company.
The report also followed a New York Times story that Huang had an extramarital relationship with another Nvidia executive. The developments sent Nvidia shares down more than 8% in after-hours trading.
Huang and Nvidia have dominated headlines since the weekend after the Nvidia CEO acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. intelligence identified as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.
Alice Huang, also known by her Chinese name Huang Le, was recruited to gather information on Jensen, according to people briefed on the intelligence cited by The New York Times.
The Nvidia chief sought to project a "business as usual" atmosphere on his first day back at the office after the revelations, but he is now facing calls to resign from several lawmakers.
Sen. Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., a member of the Senate Banking Committee, reiterated Wednesday his call for Huang to resign, joining Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee and Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress.
"As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC.

articles.title_orig: Indonesia’s vice president resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.title_zh: Indonesia’s vice president resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.content_orig:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to parliament on Thursday, triggering the process of finding his replacement amid growing turmoil for the government.
Gibran had been facing impeachment calls after a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document used during his 2024 election campaign was invalid.
His departure comes amid a faltering political alliance between his father, ex-president Joko Widodo, and the incumbent President Prabowo Subianto.
Standing alongside Gibran, Prabowo told reporters he had accepted his resignation with "a heavy heart". Lawmakers will have 60 days to fill the vacant post, choosing between two candidates named by the president.
"[Gibran] has demonstrated a chivalrous attitude, a strong sense of responsibility, and the qualities of a statesman," Prabowo said, adding that the resignation was "for the benefit of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia".
"He certainly believes that he completed his education through a proper and structured process. However, we must understand that educational systems abroad differ from those in Indonesia," the president said.
Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.
Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.
Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.
"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.
It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.
The Supreme Court ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.
Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.
On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretariat Prasetyo Hadi said.
Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.
Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.
But tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.
Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.
In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.
Last week, authorities arrested several senior officials, including presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation to Prabowo - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.
Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.
Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.
But neither man has confirmed the rift. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jokowi said he still supported Prabowo's leadership.
Jokowi also said Gibran's resignation was part of "political dynamics" and he had told his son "the position was temporary".
All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The  free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.
Across the country, students and activists have staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

Case for: Broadcom has the best setup on valuation. It trades at about 18x next-year EPS, its fair-value model shows upside, and a pullback came before this bounce. AMD has the strongest estimate momentum.
Case against: Neither stock has structurally gained from Nvidia's trouble. BofA says share gains depend on prolonged scrutiny. A quick resolution, or a strong Nov 17 report, could send money back to Nvidia. Rate risk is also growing after a hot CPI print. Read more (Nov 9, 2026)
Levels: NVIDIA (NVDA) falling below its 52-week low of $164.27 would mark a new phase of the sell-off. Broadcom (AVGO) reclaiming $350 would extend its rebound.
The data favors Broadcom's valuation setup over AMD's. Nvidia is the highest-variance case. It has the cheapest multiple and the biggest governance overhang, and there is no way to price the board's decision.

articles.title_orig: Israeli strike on hospital kills at least five Palestinians, Gaza civil defence agency says
articles.title_zh: Israeli strike on hospital kills at least five Palestinians, Gaza civil defence agency says
articles.content_orig:
At least six people have been killed and a large number injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital, the biggest hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says.
Eyewitnesses told the BBC that a single missile fired by a warplane hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units overnight.
The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions".
The Israeli military said it struck a senior Hamas figure and other operatives from the group's armed wing who had been operating within the hospital.
It alleged that they had violated international law by using the hospital as "a command centre for military and terrorist activities".
Hamas did not comment on the claim. But it accused Israel of killing patients and medical staff and perpetrating "a full-fledged war crime".
Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war.
Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies.
Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory.
In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said the missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department.
A spokesman for the Civil Defence, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry, initially said that five people had been killed and 20 others injured.
Videos shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by the blast.
Local activists have also circulated claims that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building.
Speaking to reporters in the aftermath of the strike, the director of Nasser hospital said the building had been hit in a vertical strike, causing extensive damage.
Nasser hospital was hit by a double Israeli strike in August 2025, which killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers.
Israeli strikes on Gaza have continued despite a ceasefire agreement in October last year.
More than 1,620 people have been killed since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire.
The humanitarian crisis in Gaza has recently worsened as a result of heavy rains that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title_orig: Giant statue of Roman emperor once stood in southern Scotland
articles.title_zh: Giant statue of Roman emperor once stood in southern Scotland
articles.content_orig:
A giant gilded statue of a Roman emperor once stood proudly in the heart of the Scottish Borders, new research suggests.
It had previously been assumed that a bronze leg found in a bog in Milsington near Hawick in 1820 was loot taken from a site further south - possibly York.
However, experts now believe it came from a sculpture of Antoninus Pius on horseback - similar to the one of his successor Marcus Aurelius in Rome - and was erected to mark the conquest of southern Scotland.
Dr Fraser Hunter, principal curator of prehistoric and Roman archaeology at National Museums Scotland (NMS), said: "This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome's second attempt at conquering Scotland."
The sculpture is the only known example of its kind from Scotland and has been reconstructed using its surviving leg ahead of a major new exhibition opening at NMS in Edinburgh this weekend.
The larger than life-sized lower leg with a boot dates back to about AD140 and is one of the most striking treasures from Roman Britain in the NMS collection.
A wider study of statue fragments from the Roman frontier showed that bronze imperial statues - including equestrian ones - were erected in frontier forts, thus making a Scottish location for this particular statue more feasible.
In addition, researchers said the way the leg was removed suggested the deliberate Roman dismantling of a valued sculpture as they withdrew from southern Scotland, rather than a local act of revenge.
They said it had been carefully removed, not "brutally hacked off".
Examination of the top of the leg has found that there are no cut marks, but rather it remains exactly as it was cast.
The absence of gilding around the knee shows that this area was covered by a tunic or cloak, with lumps around the top which in-filled the folds of the tunic and stuck the leg to it.
This contrasts with examples of statues being deliberately destroyed after a battle, when an emperor's memory was condemned, or when they were chopped up for scrap, typically resulting in irregular fragments on a much smaller scale.
Such careful removal and burial has been found widely in Roman Scotland when the Antonine conquests were abandoned. Examples include the burial of Antonine Wall inscriptions and the Inveresk Mithras altars, which are also on display in the exhibition.
Once curators had established that the statue was likely to have been erected in Scotland, they looked to answer the question of who it depicted.
They came to the conclusion that just one emperor paid particular heed to his Scottish victories - Antoninus Pius.
His conquest of what is now southern Scotland was the only foreign adventure that he commemorated with the title Imperator, a battle-honour meaning "commander" which marked an emperor's victory.
Hunter said: "This was a big deal for the emperor, something which was worth celebrating.
"It offers us a tantalising glimpse into the kind of grand monuments which once stood in southern Scotland and shows the importance Pius placed on his victories in Scotland.
"But it begs the question - where is the rest of the statue?".
Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire is at NMS in Edinburgh from 14 November to 18 April.
Antoninus Pius was Roman emperor for more than two decades, from AD 138 to 161.
He has been described as "mild-mannered and capable" and was the fourth of the "five good emperors" who guided the empire through an 84-year period of "internal peace and prosperity".
He succeeded Hadrian and it was during his reign that a 36-mile (58km) garrisoned barrier - the Antonine Wall - was built to extend the Roman frontier 100 miles (160km) north of Hadrian's Wall.
After his death, the empire suffered invasion by hostile tribes and civil unrest.

Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment
Senior Kremlin officials explicitly and emphatically articulated Moscow’s persistent demands for complete Ukrainian capitulation and territorial concessions that extend far beyond Donbas . Vladimir Medinsky, Russian presidential aide and head of the Russian delegation at Abu Dhabi, told Russian media outlets on November 11 that Russia will capture “every inch of [Russia’s] land one way or another.”[1] Medinsky also asserted that “wherever a Russian soldier has set foot belongs to Russia” — mirroring Russian President Vladimir Putin’s statement from June 2025.[2] Medinsky added that Russia will not accept any territorial exchanges with Ukraine and will continue to expand its “security zone” in Ukraine (very likely referring to territory in northern Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts that Russian officials claim are part of a “buffer zone.”).[3] Medinsky’s statements demonstrate the Kremlin’s territorial ambitions beyond the five illegally annexed regions in Ukraine (Crimea and Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, and Kherson oblasts) and unwillingness to engage in compromises or exchanges of territory to end the war.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov similarly stated on November 11 that Russia will pursue a “course” that fulfills the demands Putin laid out in his June 2024 speech to the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).[4] That speech required a Ukrainian withdrawal from the entirety of Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, and Kherson oblasts, including areas that Russian forces have never occupied; Ukraine’s demilitarization and “denazification” (the replacement of the current Ukrainian government with a pro-Russian one); and Ukraine’s abandonment of its NATO aspirations.[5] Kremlin officials have frequently claimed that the Ukrainian withdrawal from all of Donetsk Oblast is a necessary but insufficient condition for a peace settlement , and Putin and other high-ranking Kremlin officials have often reiterated Russia’s commitment to Putin’s June 2024 demands.[6] Ukrainian forces maintain control over 0.38 percent of Luhansk Oblast, 20.12 percent of Donetsk Oblast, 24.42 percent of Zaporizhia Oblast, and 30.11 percent of Kherson Oblast, but Putin continues to demand territory that his forces have been unable to seize.[7]
Russian officials used the Abu Dhabi talks to try to persuade US and Ukrainian officials to accept Russia’s carefully crafted fictional version of the frontline. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated on November 10 that Russian military and intelligence officials falsely claimed to the US and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi that Russian forces control half of the part of Donbas that Ukrainian forces, in reality, still control.[8] The Kremlin has long made exaggerated and grossly inaccurate claims of Russian battlefield successes.[9] The Russian MoD, in fact, regularly claims a frontline trace that does not correspond with reality at all. The Russian MoD falsely claimed the seizure of Dobropillya and Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka on October 16, for example, when Russian forces held neither settlement.[10] Putin claimed on July 3 that Russian forces had seized Kostyantynivka — a town that Russian forces have still not seized over four months later.[11] The Russian MoD repeatedly falsely claimed that Russian forces encircled Ukrainian troops in northern Kharkiv Oblast in September and October 2026.[12] Russian state media regularly publishes maps showing the fictional Russian line of claimed advances.
The Kremlin will likely continue to make false claims of advances all along the frontline in an effort to establish its fictional frontline as the basis of future negotiations on territorial issues. Russian officials often claim that peace talks need to take into consideration the “realities on the ground,” and the Kremlin is trying to push its own reality onto US, Ukrainian, and other negotiators. The Kremlin will very likely increase its claimed advances throughout Winter 2026-2027 and into Spring 2027 far beyond territories its troops can take or hold. Putin likely hopes that a devastating wintertime Russian long-range strike campaign against Ukraine will break Ukraine’s will to continue to fight and degrade Western support for Ukraine, allowing him to insist on his claimed line of advance as the starting point of any talks about a final settlement of the war.
Ukrainian and US officials in Abu Dhabi reportedly rejected Russian officials’ false claims about the battlefield, and ample evidence of Ukrainian successes in 2026 directly undermines Russia’s false narrative. Zelensky stated on November 11 that US negotiators confirmed Ukraine’s assessment of the battlefield situation — rejecting the false Russian claim that Russian forces control half of the Ukrainian-controlled territory in Donbas.[13] Russian forces have, in fact, lost the initiative and much of their offensive capabilities in several sectors of the theater throughout 2026. Russian forces have suffered a net loss of territory in four of the last eight months since the previous round of US-Ukrainian-Russian talks in February 2026, while simultaneously suffering increasingly high casualties.[14] Ukrainian forces have conducted several successful counteroffensive operations throughout 2026 in the Lyman, Oleksandrivka, and Kupyansk directions, liberating over 1,000 square kilometers of territory. Successful Ukrainian counteroffensive operations have entirely disrupted the Russian plan to seize Donetsk Oblast and created cascading effects across other sectors of the frontline, as the Russian military command had to make difficult decisions about the allocation of manpower and resources between sectors.[15] There is no basis to assess that Russian forces will be able to take the rest of Donetsk Oblast in any short period of time, as Putin continues to claim that they will, or even to forecast that Russian forces will ever be able to seize the region by force.[16]
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the Abu Dhabi talks reportedly agreed to a large-scale prisoner of war (POW) exchange. Former Senior Advisor to the US President Jared Kushner reported on November 11 that Ukrainian and Russian officials agreed to a large-scale POW exchange but noted that the parties will finalize the numbers on November 12.[17] Zelensky reported on November 11 that the delegations discussed the possibility of each side exchanging 1,000 or 1,500 POWs.[18] Russian First Deputy Chief of Information of the General Staff’s Main Directorate (GRU) Lieutenant General Alexander Zorin stated that an exchange of 1,000 POWs could take place in the next two to three weeks (around November 25 to December 2).[19] Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada (Parliament) Deputy Davyd Arakhamia stated that this POW exchange could be ”one of the biggest, if not the biggest” of the war.[20]
The US delegation will meet with Putin in Moscow City on November 12 to discuss the progress of the talks and the potential involvement of European officials in future negotiations, while the Kremlin continues to explicitly reject the idea of a multilateral format. Kushner stated on November 11 that he and US Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff will next travel to Moscow to meet with Putin in an attempt to make further progress on peace talks and to promote the idea of future European participation.[21] Kremlin Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated on November 11, however, that Russian officials currently have “no vision” of a negotiations format that includes European representatives —echoing repeated Kremlin statements in recent weeks against European involvement.[22] Kushner noted that the US delegation will also travel to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Zelensky following the visit to Moscow.[23]
The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that Alexander Darchiev, the Russian ambassador to the United States, passed away on November 11 at the age of 66. [24] Darchiev had served as ambassador since March 6,

articles.title_orig: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.title_zh: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.content_orig:
A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2 , can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618 , it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday.
Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
An attacker who can reach the server needs no authentication to exploit the flaw and could take full control of the server process, the Linux vendor says. It rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported.
HTTP/2 runs only where the Protocols directive turns it on, as the module documentation explains. The directive uses h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS and h2c for HTTP/2 over plain TCP. It can be set for the whole server or for a single virtual host, so admins should check the server-wide setting and every virtual host.
Standalone builds of the module, released on GitHub as mod_h2, are affected from version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Admins who run the Apache HTTP Server project's own releases should move to version 2.4.71, the fixed release named in its security advisory . That release also fixes a crash in mod_md, rated important, and a one-byte overwrite of stack memory in mod_vhost_alias, rated low.
The distributions in the table below ship their own builds of the server, with their own package version numbers. On Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, for example, the fix ships as mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1.
Red Hat shipped fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 yesterday and rates the flaw Important on those releases rather than Critical. Their mod_http2 packages give each HTTP/2 stream its own memory allocator, which makes an attack much harder, according to the vendor's severity assessment . Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier do not contain the vulnerable code.
The Debian rows come from Debian's security tracker , and the Amazon row from the Amazon Linux tracker . Ubuntu's CVE tracker had no page for the flaw when The Hacker News checked it today.
The Apache HTTP Server advisory offers no workaround. In its vulnerability analysis , Wiz advises admins who cannot update yet to remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive, leaving Protocols http/1.1.
The standalone mod_h2 project has published no fixed release so far. Its release list on GitHub ends at 2.0.42, the last affected version, and its repository has been read-only since it was archived on June 9. The Protocols change above also applies to servers that use those builds.
The flaw was reported on October 26 by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, a free scanning service for open-source projects that uses the company's AI models. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research reported it last week.
An earlier HTTP/2 flaw , CVE-2026-23918, was fixed in version 2.4.67, released on May 4. Servers updated to that release, or to any later one up to 2.4.70, still run a version that the new flaw affects.

articles.content_orig:
Share issuance has diluted the market and impacted investors’ returns, the US bank says
Chinese companies could unlock a further 15 per cent in equity valuation upside by stepping up share buy-backs and dividend payouts, as Beijing seeks to encourage listed firms to return more cash to investors, according to Goldman Sachs.
The US investment bank said in a report on Wednesday that an increase in corporate payout ratios and share repurchases, in line with policymakers’ efforts to improve shareholder returns, could lift valuations of the MSCI China Index by about 15 per cent from current levels through improved returns on equity and cash distributions to shareholders.
Goldman said Chinese companies had historically favoured issuing new shares over buying them back, with equity issuance outpacing repurchases for most of the past two decades.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Tumbles as Investors Consider Future Without CEO Huang
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Tumbles as Investors Consider Future Without CEO Huang
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang soon, according to two sources familiar with the matter, following allegations that Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.
The Trump administration is aware of the matter, the sources said.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on the board's moves.
Nvidia's share price slid more than 8% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the Journal's report, extending a multi-day sell-off for one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies.
The company has faced days of turmoil following reports that American intelligence agencies believed Huang was the target of a Chinese spying plot.
Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993, and for years it was best known for designing graphics cards widely used for gaming. The company now designs the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.
The New York Times reported last week on allegations that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who previously led a Singapore-based firm called Megaspeed International that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and hardware. U.S. intelligence agencies have believed for months that Alice Huang — who is not related to Jensen Huang — was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the newspaper reported.
In a message to Nvidia employees over the weekend, Jensen Huang wrote that he was "unfaithful to my wife" and apologized for hurting her and their children. He did not name the woman involved.
Nvidia's board said Sunday it had launched an independent investigation into allegations that the CEO "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said, "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the U.S. government would have notified us."
Two law enforcement sources told CBS News the Justice Department is also investigating Megaspeed over potential violations of U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI chips. Some analysts have raised questions about whether the saga resulted in China — which is racing the U.S. for AI dominance — gaining access to Nvidia's technology through Megaspeed. The company has denied any involvement in illegal chip transfers.
China has denied all allegations, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun telling reporters on Monday that the "so-called Chinese spy narrative is entirely baseless and constitutes slander and smear."
Beyond the national security concerns, Nvidia is facing a securities lawsuit accusing the company of failing to disclose information to shareholders about Jensen Huang's relationship with the alleged spy.
Jensen Huang has a close relationship with the Trump administration. President Trump gave Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 computer chips to "approved customers" in China late last year, with the federal government taking a 25% cut of chip sales. The deal did not include Nvidia's more advanced Blackwell or Rubin systems.
The Nvidia CEO and other U.S. tech executives traveled to China with Mr. Trump earlier this year.
On Monday, Mr. Trump called Jensen Huang a "very high-quality person," saying during a White House briefing that "the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape." The president said he spoke to Jensen Huang to see how he was doing, and the executive "said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."

articles.title_orig: Iran warns of expanded retaliation as Israel reportedly readies to attack
articles.title_zh: Iran warns of expanded retaliation as Israel reportedly readies to attack
articles.content_orig:
Israel has reportedly ordered its military to step up readiness for possible strikes on Iran as Tehran warned it would expand the war beyond the region if attacked.
Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the military to step up preparations for an attack on Iran, Israeli media reported on Wednesday evening.
“The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” public broadcaster KAN reported.
KAN said the directives were made public after Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot issued a statement telling Netanyahu – who is serving as prime minister in a caretaker capacity – not to deploy the military “without a direct and immediate threat” until the next government is formed.
Eisenkot was offered the chance to form a new government by Israeli President Isaac Herzog over the weekend after Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections.
Netanyahu, who is on the cusp of losing power if the opposition succeeds in forming a government, has been adamant that the war on Iran will continue until the collapse of the government in Tehran.
Reports of Israeli preparations to attack Iran come at a time of intense diplomatic efforts to avert further conflict and reach a diplomatic solution.
US President Donald Trump has said that he is prepared to return to waging war if a diplomatic track offered by Qatar fails to facilitate a deal between Washington and Tehran.
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in a social media post, “If the US launches another war against Iran, every military base involved in the aggression, from West Asia to Europe, will be a legitimate target for Iran’s lethal strikes.”
“No safe distance. No safe haven. No immunity,” he added.
Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar Atas, reporting from Tehran, said the Iranian leadership has been discussing whether or not to appoint the hawkish Rezaei as Iran’s new chief negotiator.
“In Tehran, there have been voices saying that if this status quo goes on for quite a long period of time, Iran will not wait and might take pre-emptive action,” Atas said, adding that the current lead negotiator, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has commented on Iran’s determination to move beyond this state of “no war, no peace” through “sustainable deterrence” if negotiations fail.
Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview published on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz will “never return” to its status prior to the US-Israel war on Iran and that “the ball is now in the American court”.
“What stands in the way of an agreement is our lack of trust in the United States,” he said.
In Washington, DC, Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher said Trump is still justifying why he went to war with Iran and saying that it would end soon.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also said the Trump administration’s economic pressure campaign against Iran is proving so effective that a resumption of large-scale military operations is unnecessary.
“Over the last few days, both the president and Marco Rubio have said, effectively, that large-scale military engagement is over. They do not see the need to restart it unless Iran crosses red lines,” Fisher said, adding that the “key issue for this White House is always to be in a position where Trump can declare victory”.
“But it is clear there is some movement behind the scenes as far as negotiating a settlement,” he said.
Despite the push for peace, US forces “continue to work around the clock” in keeping the Strait of Hormuz open for commercial shipping, strictly enforcing the “ironclad” naval blockade against Iran, according to the US Central Command.
Meanwhile, oil prices rose about 1 percent on Wednesday after Tehran rejected a US proposal to transfer its stockpile of 60 percent enriched uranium to a third country.
Brent futures settled $1.27, or 1.39 percent, higher at $92.76, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 49 cents, or 0.57 percent, to $86.53.
In the previous session, oil prices had initially fallen by more than $3 a barrel after US officials played down the need for further military strikes against Iran.
Prices later pared some losses when an Iranian official said no talks were taking place between the two sides.

articles.title_orig: Senior US Democratic senators urge administration to preserve Nvidia export records amid China security concerns
articles.title_zh: Senior US Democratic senators urge administration to preserve Nvidia export records amid China security concerns
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
WASHINGTON — The Trump administration has briefed top lawmakers on a growing national security crisis around the world’s leading chipmaker, Nvidia, after its chief executive, Jensen Huang, admitted over the weekend to an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy .
Senior U.S. intelligence officials briefed the Gang of Eight — congressional leaders from both parties, and the chairs and vice chairs of the House and Senate intelligence committees — on the matter, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday.
Congressional Republicans have called on Huang himself to provide an update, warning the incident raised “significant national security concerns” that could have compromised cutting-edge American technology at a critical moment in the race with China for supremacy in artificial intelligence.
Huang admitted Sunday to having an affair with Alice Huang, who was identified as a Chinese intelligence asset by U.S. authorities, after the New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had raised concerns within the administration about his potential compromise.
Nvidia’s board of directors said Sunday it will launch an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang, after he revealed he had an affair with a former Chinese executive.
President Trump is scheduled to visit China next week.
“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Jensen Huang said in a statement Sunday.
“Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports,” he added, “NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.”
Debate over export controls for the world’s most advanced semiconductor chips, produced by Nvidia, has raged over the last eight years in Washington, with lawmakers across party lines expressing concern that Chinese access to the chips could strengthen their hand in the development of the most powerful AI models.
Huang has been one of the most vocal opponents of the U.S. export controls, calling them a “mistake” and saying they were hurting American businesses more than they were constricting Chinese government efforts.
The executive was successful in lobbying the Trump administration to ease export restrictions on some of Nvidia’s most advanced chips over the past year.
Jeffries said he would be calling for greater export controls on chips after the incident. The New York congressman is expected to become the next speaker of the House after Democrats swept into power in this month’s midterm elections.
“We’re going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue,” Jeffries said, adding that “real concerns” have arisen from the case that will need to be addressed.
U.S. intelligence unmasked the Chinese intelligence operation after intercepting the communications of Alice Huang, a former journalist with Chinese state media who later became a senior executive at Megaspeed International. The Singaporean data center firm was already under the microscope for allegedly funneling restricted AI chips to Beijing.
Trump was reportedly made aware of the Chinese espionage effort targeting Huang, but chose not to act, according to the New York Times.
Nvidia’s stock dropped more than 4% Monday , after the board said it would open an investigation into its chief executive  being the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
The company “prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” it said in the statement.
Some of the world’s leading financiers are sounding increasingly alarmed about an AI bubble.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” it continued. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Rubio declined to address questions from reporters on the matter Monday.
“It’s an internal corporate matter for them, so I’m just not going to comment on that topic,” the secretary of State and national security advisor said.
But the administration could face increased calls to investigate Jensen Huang, a Trump ally, who traveled with Trump to Beijing in May and attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping in September held at the White House.
Republicans have also formally requested Huang appear before the House on Nov. 18 — when Trump will be in China — to brief them on what happened.
Rep. Brian Mast of Florida, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Rick Crawford of Arkansas, head of the House Intelligence Committee, and Rep. John Moolenaar of Michigan, who leads the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, said the issue of Chinese infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology “is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.”
“It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk,” they wrote.

articles.title_orig: The world's super-rich are piling into alternative investments. Here's why
articles.title_zh: The world's super-rich are piling into alternative investments. Here's why
articles.content_orig:
The world's wealthiest investors are increasingly looking beyond stocks and bonds, pouring money into hedge funds, private equity and infrastructure assets, as market volatility and fears about stubborn inflation spur diversification.
From Asian billionaires to global family offices, alternative investments are becoming a bigger part of portfolios once dominated by traditional assets, said industry watchers
JPMorgan Asset Management's private wealth alternative assets in Asia-Pacific surged 40% over the past 12 months, according to Dan Watkins, the firm's regional chief executive officer, underscoring the growing appetite among high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
"So you really have this huge appetite for alternative exposure happening in that ultra-high-net-worth, high-net-worth category," Watkins said recently at a media summit in Singapore.
The shift comes as investors grapple with increasingly concentrated equity markets, geopolitical uncertainty and concerns that stocks and bonds may not provide the same protection against market downturns as they once did, experts said.
"We are seeing a sharp increase in planned asset allocation to alternatives among the family offices we speak to," said John Woods, chief investment officer for Asia at Lombard Odier.
Alternative investments now account for 60% of single-family office portfolios, surpassing traditional assets for the first time, according to BNY Wealth . Traditional assets accounted for 41% of allocations, the report found.
Wealthy investors are seeking diversification, income and access to investments outside listed markets, and concerns over elevated valuations, tight credit spreads and the growing correlation between stocks and bonds have accelerated the trend, Woods added.
Hedge funds are emerging as a favored option among wealthy investors seeking protection against market swings, particularly as traditional diversification strategies face growing challenges.
Olaolu Aganga, head of portfolio construction and analytics at Citi Wealth, said hedge funds have attracted the strongest recent interest among qualified clients, who are seeking returns less dependent on the direction of equity markets.
Private credit is another area drawing interest, offering investors contractual income streams, while some hedge fund strategies seek to profit from differences in performance between companies rather than relying on broad market rallies, said Woods.
Citi's 2026 survey of 351 family offices found that inflation was their biggest concern, followed by interest rates, financial system stability and market volatility.
Wealthy families are increasingly seeking investments that can generate income and help preserve purchasing power amid persistent inflation and interest-rate uncertainty, while diversifying portfolios against market volatility, according to Aganga.
The Citi survey, however, also showed public equities recorded the strongest net increase in allocations, suggesting wealthy investors are adding alternatives rather than abandoning traditional markets. "This is not a wholesale rotation away from public markets," Woods said.
Infrastructure has emerged as another major beneficiary of the shift, with the artificial intelligence boom creating enormous demand for data centers, electricity networks and digital connectivity.
Thomas Roland Guyot, head of private markets investment specialists for Southeast Asia at UBS Unified Global Alternatives, said investors are increasingly targeting assets that support AI, electrification and energy security.
Such investments potentially offer a combination of long-term growth and relatively predictable cash flows, particularly where revenues are supported by essential demand or long-term contracts.
Investor appetite is already showing up in fund flows. Net inflows into open-ended infrastructure funds rose 30% year on year in the 12 months through the first quarter of 2026, according to PitchBook data cited by UBS.
Private equity remains a cornerstone of wealthy investors' alternative portfolios, although they are becoming more selective. Family offices are increasingly favoring direct investments in companies, co-investments alongside private equity managers and purchases of existing fund stakes on the secondary market, rather than relying solely on traditional pooled funds, according to Citi Wealth's Aganga.
Such approaches can give investors greater control over their investments or opportunities to acquire assets at discounts, said Lombard Odier's Woods.
The broader shift is also being facilitated by the growth of evergreen and semi-liquid funds, which have lowered minimum investment thresholds and reduced some administrative hurdles associated with traditional private-market funds, Woods added.
Investing into alternative assets does not come without risks, even as mitigating those is driving flows.
Private investments can lock up capital for years, while valuations may be slow to reflect deteriorating market conditions. Even funds marketed as semi-liquid can restrict withdrawals when redemption requests surge.
"Improved access does not equal liquidity," JPMorgan's Watkins said.
Citi's Aganga also warned that performance can vary significantly between managers, while private assets may appear less volatile than they actually are because valuations are updated less frequently.
Investors must also guard against unintended concentration. A portfolio holding data centers through real estate, infrastructure and private equity funds may appear diversified while remaining heavily exposed to the same AI investment cycle, UBS' Guyot said.
For now, the flow of capital into alternative assets shows their increasing appeal among the rich, though not at the expense of traditional investment, with Woods pointing out that much of the new investment is being funded by fresh capital and excess cash rather than large-scale sales of stocks and bonds.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday after the G7 Foreign Ministers' meeting in Paris, that "bad things are happening to the Iranian economy and it's unfortunate."
The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran.
As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities.
IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS
U.S. Air Force KC-135, used for in-flight refueling, takes off from RAF Mildenhall Airbase. (AP Photo/Max Nash, File)
Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said.
Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain.
Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters.
A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom .
IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY
American aircrews check a B-52 Stratofortress long-range subsonic bomber aircraft on the pan at RAF Fairford. The United Kingdom reportedly is refusing to let the United States use the base for a potential attack on Iran. (Getty Images)
The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months.
In early October, the Air Force pulled heavy bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after British counterterrorism police stopped three suspicious vans headed toward the base Sept. 27.
Two men have since been charged under the United Kingdom's National Security Act.
Separately, the Justice Department unsealed indictments against three Iranian-backed operatives on Tuesday accused of involvement in coordinated terrorist plots across Europe, including RAF Fairford.
UK POLICE ARREST 'EXPLOSIVE' SUSPECTS NEAR US AIRBASE, KEY TO IRAN WAR
The main gate of RAF Fairford is pictured on September 27, 2026 in Fairford, United Kingdom. Police declared a major incident after evacuating residents from their homes in Whelford, a village about one mile from RAF Fairford, a military base that hosts U.S. Air Force bombers involved in the Iran conflict. (David Bown/Getty Images)
RAF Mildenhall is home to the 100th Air Refueling Wing, the only permanently based U.S. tanker wing in Europe.
Its KC-135 Stratotankers support allied aerial refueling and long-range strike missions across the region.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that Washington routinely repositions military forces.
"We are constantly repositioning forces around the world for a variety of reasons," Rubio told reporters when asked about the evacuation.

articles.title_orig: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.title_zh: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week that illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, two people familiar with the matter told CNN.
Trump officials have long harbored concerns that Megaspeed has circumvented US law and funneled advanced chips into China — a prospect that Treasury staffers argued should land it on Commerce’s so-called entity list of China-connected companies that could pose national security risks. But the issue gathered newfound attention and importance in recent days when Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Megaspeed employee suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Senior Trump officials, including Lutnick, also were briefed months ago about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who the intelligence community suspected of being a Chinese spy, people familiar with the matter said.
But despite those warnings, Commerce has so far refused to put Megaspeed on the entity list, the people said.
Confronted on it by Bessent last Thursday, Lutnick did not immediately commit to taking any specific action, they said.
Axios first reported the Situation Room confrontation.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company that was originally incorporated in 2015 as a Chinese video game developer called 7Road International. But in the three years since Alice Huang became director and the company changed its name, it has become one of the largest buyers of Nvidia chips in Asia , purchasing more than $4 billion worth of its semiconductors, by some analyst estimates.
Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing and said it is a “compliant and legal company.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”
The entity list represents one of the US’s most significant tools for preventing American firms from selling their products to foreign companies and organizations. But adding Megaspeed to the list could also risk inflaming tensions with China amid Trump’s efforts to manage the US’ trade relationship with the fellow superpower. The Commerce Department hasn’t added any company to the list in more than a year.
Representatives for the Treasury and Commerce departments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Futures Fall As Nvidia May Oust CEO Huang; Spoils Big AI-Led Rally?
articles.title_zh: Futures Fall As Nvidia May Oust CEO Huang; Spoils Big AI-Led Rally?
articles.content_orig:
Huang admitted in a statement to the company he was "unfaithful" to his wife.
The Nvidia board is reportedly planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman and alleged spy and another with an executive at his tech company.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future with the technology giant he founded.
ABC News has reached out to Nvidia for comment.
On Sunday, Nvidia said that its board launched an independent investigation "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."
The development on Wednesday comes after The New York Times reported nearly two weeks ago that Huang had "a close relationship" with an alleged Chinese government agent, identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed. He later admitted in an internal statement to Nvidia staff that he had been "unfaithful to his wife."
Amid the fallout from the allegations and the letter, The Times reported on Wednesday that Huang also allegedly had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who allegedly reports to him.
The outlet, citing sources within the company, reported that Huang and his colleague were allegedly captured on video being affectionate at a hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. The New York Times said it had not seen the video.
ABC News has not been able to verify the reporting or the alleged video.
Following the reporting about Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who are not related, the Chinese government denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment after the New York Times story broke.
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected" and are part of Jensen Huang's job, an Nvidia spokesperson told ABC News at the time.
On Sunday, Nvidia shared with ABC News the internal message Jensen Huang sent to employees, in which he said he was "unfaithful," apologizing for hurting his wife and family.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the message said, in part. It did not name Alice Huang nor any other person.
Addressing Nvidia staff, partners and shareholders, Huang went on to say, "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," Huang's message said.
Following the New York Times report, congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China sent a letter to Jensen Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang.
The Republican chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Brian Mast, told ABC News on Tuesday that he's prepared to subpoena Huang if he does not respond by Wednesday to a request from several House Republicans.
President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that he spoke with Huang that day about the allegations.
"I asked him that question -- 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy,' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
In its statement on Sunday, Nvidia said that a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement further said.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," according to the statement.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement further said.
"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," according to the statement.
Nvidia has grown to be one of the most important chip makers in recent years due to its components being key to AI computing servers.

Russia’s chief negotiator ⁠at Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi Vladimir ⁠Medinsky said ​after their conclusion that mutual understanding ⁠had been achieved on some issues and that more ⁠talks would be held.
Medinsky, ​in ‌remarks broadcast ‌on Russian state television, said that ‌ Russia and Ukraine had agreed on a large-scale prisoner swap, the latest in a long line of ‌such exchanges.
He was cool however on the ​prospect of European countries joining the talks and said it was unclear what ⁠there was for Russia and the ​European ​Union to ​discuss, given what he ​said ‌was a lack ​of ​proposals from the European side, Reuters reported.
And, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today .
US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin in Moscow and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin on Thursday as they hope to progress some issues discussed during trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi today ( 12:44 ).
The three sides have agreed on a large-scale prisoner swap and made some technical progress in their talks ( 12:30 ), but US envoys conceded there is “no trust between the sides.”
The US also appears to be pushing for Europe to be formally included in the process, with Kushner saying he would seek Putin’s “blessing” for such a move tomorrow ( 12:51 ).
Ukraine’s president Zelenskyy insisted that Europe “must be represented” at the talks ( 14:28 ), a point he also made in a speech to the Danish parliament earlier today ( 12:23 ).

In further comments to Russia’s Vesti news, Medinsky said there is no prospect of territorial exchanges between Russia and Ukraine as part of a peace deal.
“The topic of possible territorial exchanges is periodically raised from various sides,” Medinsky said.
“After Ukraine’s invasion of the Kursk region, a decision was made – the president has spoken about this repeatedly – to create a security zone along the border with Russia . This zone is now quite substantial, it is expanding, and will continue to expand. I see no possibility of exchanging these territories.”
He was referring to Ukraine’s incursion into Russia’s Kursk region in August 2024 , when Ukrainian forces crossed the border and seized territory in one of the most significant cross-border operations of the war. Zelenskyy said at the time that the operation was aimed at creating a buffer zone to protect communities in Ukraine’s neighbouring Sumy region from Russian attacks. The incursion was also widely seen as potentially giving Kyiv leverage in future negotiations.
Maria Zakharova, a spokesperson for the ⁠Russian foreign ministry, has a message for the UK defence secretary Wes Streeting – call us and let’s talk.
That’s according to a Reuters report of a Russian foreign ministry briefing today. Zakharova was responding to Streeting’s comments in an interview with the Financial Times , in which he called for additional channels of communication between the two countries, particularly direct military-to-military contact, to avoid “miscalculation”.
“I can confidently recommend ​that the British ‌defence secretary contact the ‌Russian ministry of defence. They’ll pick up the phone ‌and have a conversation ,” Zakharova said.
Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian delegation participating in peace talks with the US and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, has again signalled cautious optimism over the prospects of reaching an agreement to end the war.
Speaking to the Russian news outlet Vesti, he was asked whether the countries were any closer to achieving peace. He replied:
double quotation mark I think so. Much depends on Ukraine, the position of the United States, and whether Europe comes to its senses. In any case, all the goals we set will be achieved. ”
We reported earlier ( see post at 11.30am ) that Medinsky had said the discussions resulted in mutual understanding on several issues, with both sides agreeing to hold further talks and carry out a large-scale prisoner exchange.
Thousands of people are marching through Warsaw to mark the 108th anniversary of Poland regaining independence in 1918.
The annual march which brings together thousands of Poles remains deeply divisive, given some violent clashes in the past and the attendance of nationalist and far-right groups from Poland and abroad.
But despite regular criticism, the march has in recent years become increasingly mainstream, taking the role of the largest mass independence day celebration in the country and attracting more conservative Poles to take part.
Poland’s conservative president Karol Nawrocki was seen walking in today’s procession, which organisers hoped would attract up to 500,000 people.
By mid-afternoon, no major incidents had been reported, other than the widespread use of red flares along the route of the march, Poland’s state broadcaster TVP Info reported.
As Reuters noted, organisers argued that the ⁠gathering, held under the motto “A Pole is the host in Poland,” is their way of expressing national pride.
“We want a sovereign Poland, independent of foreign capitals ... We also ​envision a Poland that ​is as monoethnic as possible,” a spokesperson for the march organisers Rafał Buca said.
Poland’s centrist prime minister Donald Tusk – a regular target of chants, banners and often abusive taunts at the march – stayed clear of the event, attending a smaller celebration in Szczecin instead.
“I ‌address everyone, including those who will be gathering in Warsaw. We may hold different views, ‌we may keep each other in check, and at times we may even be political opponents; yet, anyone who truly cares about Poland must understand that this space, defined by independence, freedom, and a secure Republic, is a common good,” he said.
The march comes less than a year before the 2027 parliamentary election, which will see the current centrist government, led by Donald Tusk, face a group of conservative, nationalist and libertarian right parties in what is likely to be a polarising, bruising contest.
Opposition leader and former prime minister Jarosław Kaczyński told Onet that he hoped to maintain the unity of right-wing forces ahead of the election, despite the fact that “even today, during this march, there are some unpleasant elements.”
Bulgaria is marking a day of national mourning today after eleven people died and more than 50 were injured in a mass pileup in thick fog on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, AFP reported.
Crashes snared around 50 cars and trucks heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency.
The incident took place in thick fog, drastically reducing visibility for drivers.
Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures.

articles.title_orig: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns
articles.title_zh: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns
articles.content_orig:
Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says
The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.
Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year.
This level of warming smashes the 1.5C threshold that was agreed by countries a decade ago but is set to be breached in just a few years. Scientists have warned that beyond this point already harmful storms, droughts, heatwaves, flooding and other impacts will become intolerable for parts of the world and potentially trigger runaway climate change that won’t be contained.
Countries, minus the US , are gathered in the Turkish city of Antalya for UN climate talks that have centred on the looming “overshoot” of the temperature target. This reality should compel governments to act quickly to phase out use of the fossil fuels that are causing the climate crisis, the UN secretarygeneral, António Guterres, said on Tuesday .
If countries did act decisively to slash emissions then the future temperature projections would become less daunting, the CAT report states. However, in even the most optimistic scenario – where all pledges, targets and other long-term promises made by countries were fulfilled – the world would still heat up by 1.9C by the end of the century.
Such targets have been routinely flouted by the countries that have made them, however. This means leaders face a crunch moment, experts say.
“The stark choice for governments is to either continue to support the fossil fuel industry, which would consign humanity to insurmountable economic damages, rising mortality from heat and climate-driven diseases and disasters that they are unable to adapt to – or pivot to the solutions which are available and cheaper than ever,” says Bill Hare, chief executive of CAT partner organisation Climate Analytics.
Hare said exceeding 1.5C warming “cannot be an excuse to open the door to defeatism” and that every small increment of temperature rise will be significant. The CAT analysis is similar to one recently put out by the UN , which uses previous CAT data to inform its own projections.
While the world is failing to cut emissions in line with the science and countries’ own promises, carbon pollution is set to dip slightly this year and CAT pointed to some causes for optimism. Clean energy investment is now double that of fossil fuels, electric car use is soaring and the deforestation of the Amazon in Brazil has fallen sharply .
But much more will need to be done to avert disastrous climate impacts. Greta Thunberg, the Swedish climate advocate, arrived in Antalya on Tuesday and warned that “everything and everyone we love is at stake” because of the failure to confront the climate crisis.
“Governments collectively are simply not moving fast enough to adopt the policies that would enable us to escape from the emerging overshoot trap,” said Sarah Heck, lead author of the CAT report. Some countries, such as the US, Canada and New Zealand, are even slowing down their climate action to a “staggering level”, she added.
